I'm a mathematician and statistician at the **University of Arkansas at Little
Rock**, where I teach undergraduate and graduate courses and direct the Math
Assistance Center. Most of my work sits at the intersection of:

- **Bayesian statistics** — particularly robust Bayesian model-averaged
  meta-analysis and methods that take publication bias seriously.
- **Teaching** — designing courses and materials that emphasize conceptual
  understanding and reproducibility over rote procedure.
- **Reproducible workflows** — R, Quarto, LaTeX, and Git as everyday tools,
  not just research artifacts.

## Outside the classroom

Away from the desk I climb — mostly **bouldering**, the short, powerful
problems that reward patience, reading a sequence carefully, and trying again
after falling. Closer to home I **garden** and tinker with small homesteading
projects, do a fair amount of **woodworking and building**, and help look
after a small menagerie of animals with my wife, Jenn.

The common thread is practical problem-solving and durable, low-fuss systems —
the same instinct that shows up in a reproducible analysis pipeline, a raised
bed that survives the summer, or a boulder problem worked out one move at a
time. A lot of the visual language on this site — stone, crystal, ridgeline —
comes from that side of life.
